text_en: The Government has mapped 718 services for businesses and citizens, of which 276 are digitally available.
summary: The Government has mapped 718 services for businesses and citizens, of which 276 are available digitally.

text_en: The Public Administration Reform (PAR) Strategy 2023-2030 focuses on de-bureaucratisation, digitalisation and better service delivery through a network of one-stop shops, and the State Chancellery is the main policymaker in the service delivery area.
summary: The PAR Strategy 2023-2030 focuses on de-bureaucratisation, digitalisation and service delivery through one-stop shops; the State Chancellery leads service delivery policy.
extraction_note: The passage describes the strategy without stating whether it is adopted or implemented; the executive summary (page 7) says the Government has enacted a new PAR strategy but not implemented it yet.

text_en: The recently amalgamated (February 2023) Ministry of Economic Development and Digitalisation (MEDD), for which a detailed role is currently being defined, deals with wider aspects of the digital society and economy.
summary: The Ministry of Economic Development and Digitalisation, merged in February 2023, handles the digital society and economy; its detailed role is still being defined.

text_en: Three key executive agencies under the State Chancellery – the Public Services Agency (PSA), the Electronic Governance Agency (EGA) and the Information Techn ology and Cyber Security Service (ITCSS) – each have a clear role to play in service delivery modernisation.
summary: The Public Services Agency, the Electronic Governance Agency and the IT and Cyber Security Service each have a clear role in modernising service delivery.

text_en: Of the 714 services the Government has mapped for businesses and citizens (mid-August 2023), 283 are digitally available.
summary: Of 714 services mapped by mid-August 2023, 283 are available digitally.
extraction_note: The figures differ from the 718 and 276 given on pages 9 and 99.

text_en: Regarding digital services, 52% of citizens and 60% of businesses are satisfied.
summary: 52% of citizens and 60% of businesses are satisfied with digital services.

text_en: Base registers are connected through the technical interoperability solution MConnect
summary: Base registers are connected through the MConnect interoperability solution.
extraction_note: The sentence continues on page 97 ("the use of which is growing quickly .") after a running footer ("Service delivery") that the quote check does not skip, so the quote stops at the end of the main clause on page 96; the growth claim is covered by the next item.

text_en: In the year after  MConnect’s launch in 2019, about 18.5 million transactions were conducted, while in 2022 the number of transactions reached 665.7 million.
summary: MConnect handled about 18.5 million transactions in the year after its 2019 launch and 665.7 million in 2022.

text_en: The Government is planning to bring more state bodies and private entities into the MConnect system.
summary: The Government plans to connect more state bodies and private entities to MConnect.
intervention_as_stated: extension of the MConnect system to more state bodies and private entities

text_en: E -signature is in place and there are 200 000 active users, mostly for businesses purposes, represent ing 9.8% of Moldova’s adult  population.
summary: Electronic signature has 200 000 active users, mostly for business purposes, or 9.8% of the adult population.

text_en: A more user -friendly smart phone-based e- signature platform (MobiSign) is also being  prepared.
summary: A more user-friendly smartphone-based e-signature platform, MobiSign, is being prepared.

text_en: The PSA has also begun  to provide a front-office function for other government service providers, with two portals in use: servicii.gov.md is a comprehensive administrative services portal, while e-services.md offers PSA services only and is therefore quite limited in coverage.
summary: Two portals are in use: servicii.gov.md covers administrative services comprehensively, while e-services.md offers only Public Services Agency services.

text_en: A lthough guidelines are in place,  Government websites comply poorly with intern ational accessibility standards.
summary: Despite guidelines, government websites comply poorly with international accessibility standards.
extraction_note: Accessibility of government websites to WCAG standards: unclear whether this meets the materiality test for digital government (online channel accessibility rather than a digital service itself).

text_en: When surveyed, 48% of respondents claimed to be  satisfied with public services across the territory, and 63% are satisfied with accessibility to public services via digital channels.
summary: 48% are satisfied with public services across the territory and 63% with access to public services through digital channels.

text_en: 2. The Government should establish a standard approach for service re- design and automation which is based on life events and identifying legal, technological and organisational barriers across agencies, and aims to redesign the services driven by user convenience.
summary: Short-term: the Government should set a standard, life-event-based approach to redesigning and automating services, identifying legal, technological and organisational barriers.
extraction_note: Service redesign is mainly administrative simplification; automation and technological barriers make the digital element part of the subject, but it is not the only subject.

text_en: 3. The Government should integrate the individual PSA portal “e- services” to the comprehensive government portal “servicii.gov” to encompass all services of all central government services into a single portal.
summary: Short-term: the Government should merge the Public Services Agency portal e-services into servicii.gov so all central government services are on one portal.

text_en: 4. The State Chancellery should categorise digital services according to their maturity level and keep account of the services accordingly.
summary: Short-term: the State Chancellery should categorise digital services by maturity level and keep account of them accordingly.

text_en:
2. Existence and extent of application of policy on digital service delivery  8/8 
3. Central co-ordination for digital government projects  4/4
summary: SIGMA scores Moldova 8 of 8 for its digital service delivery policy and 4 of 4 for central co-ordination of digital government projects.

text_en: Under the heading “De-bureaucratisation and the Development of Electronic Services”, it covers a general objective and three priority directions: 1) 100% modernised public services; 2) a well -established e-Government ecosystem; and 3) digit alised local public administration.
summary: The PAR Strategy 2023-2030 includes a heading on electronic services with three directions: modernised services, an e-Government ecosystem and digitalised local administration.
extraction_note: “it” refers to the PAR Strategy 2023-2030 named in the preceding sentence. Status not stated in the passage.
intervention_as_stated: PAR Strategy 2023-2030, heading “De-bureaucratisation and the Development of Electronic Services”

text_en: In addition to the PAR Strategy 2023-2030, MEDD has prepared a Digital Transformation Strategy 2023- 2030 to develop a digital society and economy, but establishing an  intelligent and transparent digital state is also one of its  objectives.
summary: The Ministry of Economic Development and Digitalisation has prepared a Digital Transformation Strategy 2023-2030, which also aims at an intelligent, transparent digital state.
extraction_note: Status proposed: the next sentence calls it a draft strategy.

text_en: While the draft strategy emphasis es principles and technological solutions for digital governance, it also overlaps with the PAR Strategy.
summary: The draft Digital Transformation Strategy emphasises digital governance principles and solutions but overlaps with the PAR Strategy.

text_en: Since February 2023, however, incorporation of the position of Deputy Prime Minister for Digitalisation into MEDD has required extra attention to ensure that digitalisation efforts remain aligned with broader PAR Strategy objectives, and that accountability for results is clear.
summary: Since February 2023, moving the Deputy Prime Minister for Digitalisation into the ministry requires extra attention to keep digitalisation aligned with PAR and accountability clear.

text_en: While the PSA and EGA work jointly on reeng ineering and digitalising services, constant political support is needed to introduce more radical legal and redesign solutions to  challenge existing practices by decisively eliminating unnecessary steps or entire services to make them more citizen- friendly.
summary: The Public Services Agency and e-Governance Agency jointly reengineer and digitalise services; constant political support is needed for more radical legal and redesign solutions.
extraction_note: “is needed” could be read as a barrier (lack of political support) or a recommendation; recommendation chosen. The digital element is joint digitalisation work, but the subject is administrative simplification.

text_en: For example, some services, such as applying for a construction permit in the city of Chisinau, have been digitalised but only partially, resulting in a double burden for applicants who have to print out materials from a designated information system to get approval signatures from various authorities, then scan and upload the documents into the system again.
summary: Some services, such as Chisinau construction permits, are only partly digitalised, so applicants must print, sign, scan and re-upload documents.

text_en: Approximately 38% of all services have been brought online.
summary: About 38% of all services have been brought online.

text_en: Of the 718 services currently listed in the register of public services,  276 e- services are available through the portal servicii.gov.md.
summary: 276 of the 718 services in the register of public services are available as e-services through servicii.gov.md.

text_en: Moldova scored 0.72 out of 1 on the United Nations' 2022 E -Government Development Index , placing it 72nd out of 193 countries.
summary: Moldova scored 0.72 on the UN 2022 E-Government Development Index, ranking 72nd of 193 countries.

text_en: While Moldova has made progress in recent years, it has not managed to close the gap with the EU average, as the difference in the 2022 index (about 15 percentage points) is similar to the difference in 2018.
summary: Moldova has not closed its e-government index gap with the EU average, about 15 points in 2022 as in 2018.

text_en: The country finds it particularly difficult to provide high-quality services to its citizens: in 2022, the score for service delivery provision was just 0.69.
summary: Moldova's 2022 e-government score for service delivery provision was 0.69.
